# Current state — exprim

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Policies

### Local documents are cited as secrets, never named in tracked files

`proposed` · `@exprim.privacy.private-document-references/1` · scope `all`

No tracked file, commit message or ledger record names a private local
document: not its path, its file name, its title, or the directory it
lives in. Where a document or directory must be referred to, register the
value with `akr secret put` and write the returned citation instead.
Published corpus manifests identify a private document by a neutral id
(`map-b`, `shading-a`), its size and its SHA-256 only.

Working notes (`dev-notes/`) and benchmark results (`docs/benchmarks/`)
stay on the machine, git-ignored: they describe private documents by
nickname, title and page image. Findings that should be public go into
this ledger or the changelog, with documents described by kind.

Files that need real paths at run time stay untracked:
`tools/render-probe/g0-corpus.local.json` and
`tools/render-bench/corpus.local.json`. Scripts take directories from
the environment or from those local files.

### Peak memory after the 2026-11-20 fixes, same fixtures and method as the audit

`verified` · `@exprim.memory.peak-after-20261120/1` · scope `path "src/content/**"`, `path "src/document/**"`, `path "src/print/**"`, `path "src/reader/session.rs"`, `path "src/render_cpu/**"`, `path "src/render_scheduler/**"`, `path "src/structure/decode.rs"`

Measured on the uncommitted working tree over the commit below, with the same probe, machine and fixtures as the audit (peak working set, debug-fast build). Before to after:

- 200 repeats of one page-sized clip (corpus/vector/clip-repeat.pdf): 216 to 15 MB at 144 dpi, 911 to 44 MB at 300 dpi, 3,616 to 158 MB at 600 dpi. Warm render cycles fall 90 to 95 percent.
- Four synthetic clip pages rendered in turn at 600 dpi (repeated, nested, 48 distinct large, twelve deep): 1,223 to 406 MB. The remainder is the surface plus one mask budget of eight page-sized planes.
- A page-sized opaque non-isolated wrapper group at 600 dpi: 260 to 140 MB; nested wrappers with a clip inside, 269 to 171 MB.
- 200-page document with a slow first page through the scheduler at default options: 2,616 to 688 MiB at 300 dpi, 637 to 393 MiB at 2x, wall time unchanged (2.06 s and 2.09 s at 2x).
- One 4000x5000 RGB Flate image on a 1.9 MB page: 128 to 74 MB (the decoded image is 60 MB). Sixty pages sharing that image through the scheduler: 725 to 327 MiB working set, 992 to 327 MiB commit, 948 to 265 ms; with one compile and one render worker, 245 to 100 MiB.
- Unchanged, as expected: a plain page (140 MB at 600 dpi), stroke-dense pages (the lowered arena is untouched: 218 MB for round-contours), tiling and non-wrapper groups (309 MB for pattern-shade-alpha), and the session RGB path's 241 MB at the packing instant.

Identity: page hashes equal the pre-change build on 24 documents (the public vector, text and shading fixtures, three synthetic clip, group and image documents and one large-image page) at four scales, RGBA and Gray8, through a fresh backend, a reused backend and the parallel scheduler: 576 configurations, 0 differ, also with the clip-mask budget forced to zero. The workspace suite passes (78 test binaries, 1,285 tests). Not covered by any of this: codec images (DCT, JPX, JBIG2, CCITT) in a page-hash comparison, real documents, a real printer, and CUPS beyond a type check.

The sixty-page figure is still several copies of the image: compiles that do not overlap in time do not share, and compiled pages carry their samples through the queue.

### Where peak memory goes: clip masks, reorder window, compile-time image inflation, session RGB path

`verified` · `@exprim.memory.peak-audit-20261120/1` · scope `path "src/content/**"`, `path "src/print/**"`, `path "src/reader/session.rs"`, `path "src/render_cpu/**"`, `path "src/render_scheduler/**"`, `path "src/structure/decode.rs"`

Peak working set measured with tools/render-probe (debug-fast build, Windows, 20 logical cores) on the public corpus/vector fixtures and three throwaway synthetic PDFs. A US Letter RGBA surface is 7.8 MB at 144 dpi, 33.7 MB at 300 dpi, 134.7 MB at 600 dpi; a page with nothing else going on peaks about 5 MB above its surface (page-rects 140 MB at 600 dpi).

1. Clip masks. clip-repeat.pdf (55 KB, one circular clip re-established 200 times) peaks at 216 MB / 911 MB / 3.62 GB at 144 / 300 / 600 dpi. The profiling counter render.clip.mask_bytes reads 3.47 GB in 200 prebuilt masks, while peak_live_bytes reports 134.7 MB: the engine's own peak counter does not see masks. Every consumed mask is built up front once a page has 16 or more, kept until the page ends, never shared between identical clip paths, not bounded by RenderLimits.max_page_bytes (2 GiB) and absent from the scheduler's job estimate.

2. Reorder window. A 200-page document whose first page is slow (6,000 round-joined strokes; other pages one rectangle) through RenderScheduler::render_range at default options (7 compile + 13 render workers, window 80) peaks at 637 MiB at scale 2 and 2,616 MiB at 300 dpi: 79 finished surfaces waiting behind page 0. The permit is released when the render returns, so the 4 GiB memory_limit_bytes never binds; the page-count window does. A slow emit callback fills the window the same way.

3. Non-codec images. A page drawing one 4000x5000 RGB Flate image at scale 1 (1.9 MB surface) peaks at 123 MiB: the image is inflated in full at compile time whatever the render scale, into a doubling Vec, then copied by Arc::from(Vec). Sixty pages sharing that one image XObject peak at 725 MiB working set (992 MiB commit): each compile inflates its own copy and the compiled page carries it through the queue and the render. The SharedImageCache never sees these images; only codec images (DCT, JPX, JBIG2, CCITT) go through it.

4. Session RGB path. One 600 dpi page through RenderSession peaks at 241 MB against 140 MB through CpuBackend directly: the RGBA surface and a fresh RGB plane are alive together (7 bytes per pixel). Afterwards the RGBA buffer stays parked in a thread-local worker context, with up to two further sizes (128 MiB each) in a second thread-local; neither is released when the session is dropped. Gray8 through either API peaks at 174 MB (RGBA plus the gray plane).

5. Lowered display list. Lowering flattens the whole page before any pixel is painted. round-contours.pdf at 600 dpi holds 7.66 M points and 766 k subpaths, 84 MB of arena beside a 135 MB surface (peak 218 MB); dashed-contours holds 28 MiB of capacity for 18.8 MB used. Subpath ranges are (usize, usize), 16 bytes each.

6. Read, not measured. A non-isolated group with Normal blend, opacity 255 and no soft mask in force is rendered on a seeded offscreen and copied back row by row (composite_group_seeded), so it could paint on its parent directly. The scheduler's group estimate is in user units at 1x (not scaled by the transform), Gray8 jobs are charged 1 byte per pixel against 5 actual, and the image term takes the largest image although every image decoded during lowering stays alive until the page finishes. All three print spoolers call compose_sheet (whole sheet accumulated) and the Windows spooler then builds a second full BGR copy. CpuBackendOptions.tile_size is never read: there is no banded execution.

Already done, not a finding: the bilevel summed-area table is test-only (replaced by the row-band popcount); the image cache is single-flight with one global bound; baseline JPEG streams by MCU row.

### On large real scans the whole file is read at open; render-side changes are hash-identical there

`verified` · `@exprim.memory.real-documents-20261120/1` · scope `path "src/render_cpu/**"`, `path "src/source/**"`, `path "src/structure/loader.rs"`

The twenty largest PDFs of a local test directory (12 to 781 MB; scanned books with JPEG 2000, JPEG, JBIG2 and CCITT images, one mixed-raster-content book, some vector and text documents) were rendered with a probe built before any of the 2026-11-20 changes and with the current tree.

Identity: first six pages of 19 documents at scales 0.5 and 1.0, RGBA and Gray8, fresh backend, reused backend and the parallel scheduler: 228 configurations, 0 differ, with the default chunk size and with a flush after every op. The mixed-raster-content book (eight pages, three scales): 18 configurations, 0 differ, also with the chunk size and the clip-mask budget forced to zero. This is the first identity check of these changes on codec images.

Peak working set, six pages in turn on one thread at 150 dpi, before and now: unchanged to within 1 percent on 16 of 19 documents (for example 1,171 and 1,171 MB; 404 and 405 MB), lower on three (603 to 565, 275 to 269, 55 to 51 MB). The mixed-raster-content book: 302 and 300 MB. Through the scheduler that book varies from 360 to 470 MiB run to run in both builds, so no difference is measurable there.

What dominates on the large scans is not rendering. After open, before any page is rendered, the working set equals the file size (787 MB for a 781 MB file, 584 for 578, 298 for 292, 244 for 238) while committed memory is 2 to 4 MB, and open takes 0.6 to 1.9 s. In the file examined, startxref points at binary data, so the loader falls back to searching the whole file backwards for the xref keyword, byte by byte, through the memory map. The pages are file-backed and can be dropped by the operating system, but they are resident, and a session opened from in-memory bytes holds them outright. Rendering one page then adds 12 to 28 MB of committed memory.

An intermediate build regressed the mixed-raster-content book from 302 to 391 MB over eight pages. Two causes, both fixed: the buffer pool kept one buffer per distinct page size (the pages all differ), and chunked rendering allocated the page surface before lowering, so it sat beside each image decode.

### Where CPU render time goes on dense vectors, tables and text (G0)

`verified` · `@exprim.renderer.attribution-20261110/3`

Measured on a 38-document corpus with stage timers, work counters and
sampled profiles (full report kept locally, not published):

- Dense map anchor: 72% of render time was tiling patterns. 60
  pattern-painted draws became 79,447 tile instances while 11% of the
  tiled pixels were visible through the draws' shapes.
- Clip masks: one page spent 96% of 4.3 s rasterizing 27.5 million rows
  to build 7,002 masks of about 6 KB each.
- Vector tables: 62% of render time was the compact kernel sweeping
  every interior cell of plain rectangles.
- Strokes and curves: every cubic takes 16 segments and every round join
  a 16-gon at every flattened vertex; on a stroke-heavy diagram 80% of
  edges are join disks and 97% of interior vertices are smooth.
- Text: a warm page is 56% glyph-cache lookup during lowering and 30%
  blits; through RenderSession 47% is RGBA to RGB packing.
- Compile is outside warm figures but is 36.5% of a first pass over
  table pages and 22.4% over text pages.
- After the G1 changes the map is 55% coverage kernel and 24% lowering;
  the tile cull test is 5.7%; about 10% of samples are under the
  allocator; libm rounding is 1.5% and trig 0.1%.

Absolute times drifted with machine load during the session; shares and
paired ratios are the reliable figures.

**supersedes** `@exprim.renderer.attribution-20261110/2`
